utility.notes: The City of Fullerton's own Utility Services Division page describes that division's scope as water, sanitation, sewer, and trash billing only, with no electric utility function, and the city's own Energy Conservation page promotes SCE's CARE & FERA discount programs to residents — both consistent with SCE (not the city) being the electric utility. Fullerton's site also has a page titled 'Public Utilities Commission,' a naming trap verified separately to cover only water/sanitation/sewer/trash, not electric.

value.notes: Fullerton's own city government site hosts a page titled 'Orange County Power Authority | Fullerton, CA' (S10), confirming a formal OCPA relationship exists, though cityoffullerton.com returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch (same as every other Fullerton page this session) so its exact content could not be read. OCPA's own domain (ocpower.org) returned server errors (500/502) on every page attempted this session — a genuine outage, not a deliberate block. Fullerton's OCPA membership is corroborated by multiple independent sources (OCPA's own newsroom coverage and a peer member city's official site) consistently naming Fullerton as an OCPA member city since 2021-2022. Confidence reflects that this is indirect corroboration, not a directly-read primary-source page, unlike Irvine's generation_supplier record.

value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Explicitly available to both PG&E and SCE residential customers per the statewide SGIP administrator; SCE administers it within its own distribution territory, which includes Fullerton/Orange County.
